A wallet balance is not just a number in a database.

Suppose customers can fund a wallet using USD, EUR, GBP, INR, BTC, ETH, USDC or USDT—but the wallet always maintains:

1 Wallet Unit = USD 1

The correct internal flow should be:

Funding received

→ Settlement confirmed

→ Compliance screening

→ Currency or crypto converted

→ Double-entry journal posted

→ USD wallet balance credited

→ External funds reconciled

The architecture requires:

  • Wallet orchestration
  • Fiat and crypto deposit services
  • FX and liquidity engine
  • Immutable double-entry ledger
  • Holds and available-balance controls
  • Withdrawal and payout orchestration
  • Treasury and reserve monitoring
  • Automated reconciliation

A few rules should remain non-negotiable:

  • Never credit the wallet on a pending payment
  • Never let an admin directly edit a balance
  • Redis or cache must not become the money source of truth
  • Every callback must be idempotent
  • Corrections must use reversal entries
  • Customer wallet liabilities must remain fully backed

Blockchain can be used as a funding and settlement rail, but the authoritative wallet ledger should remain on the internal server.
